covered_actors: Heads of all Executive Branch departments and agencies defined in 44 U.S.C. § 3502(1), including independent regulatory agencies (44 U.S.C. § 3502(5)) (excluding National Security Systems; Intelligence Community elements exempt from Section 4(a)-(b) and inventory duties; CFO Act agencies subject to additional Strategy and Governance Board mandates)
Agency Chief AI Officers (CAIOs), Agency AI Governance Boards, and the OMB-chaired interagency Chief AI Officer Council
Federal AI and AI-enabling workforce, agency risk-accepting officials, and internal independent agency reviewers
Vendors providing AI products or services to covered Federal agencies
prohibited_practices: Continuing to operate high-impact AI functionality that is not compliant with Section 4(b) minimum risk management practices (agencies must safely discontinue or cease use if proper risk mitigation is not possible and no CAIO waiver applies)
Vendor use of Federal Government data to train or improve commercial AI offerings without express agency permission (recommended contractual restriction)
Developers or vendors directly relying on validation or test datasets to train AI systems

evidence.quote: Complete AI Impact Assessment. Agencies must complete an AI impact assessment before deploying any high-impact AI use case. These assessments must be updated periodically and throughout the AI' s lifecycle, as appropriate, using target variables that anticipate real-world outcomes.

results ofindependent review, supported by an independent reviewer within the agency who has not been involved in the development. The independent reviewer of the impact assessment shall identify any potential concerns or gaps.
Conduct Pre-Deployment Testing. Agencies must develop pre-deployment testing and prepare risk mitigation plans that reflect expected real-world outcomes and identify expected benefits to the AI use.

Agencies must conduct testing and periodic human review of AI use cases, where feasible, to identify any adverse impacts to the performance and security of AI functionality, including those that may violate laws governing privacy, civil rights, or civil liberties.

Provide Additional Human Oversight, Intervention, and Accountability. Agencies must ensure human oversight, intervention, and accountability suitable for high-impact use cases. When practicable and consistent with existing agency practices, agencies must ensure that the AI functionality has an appropriate fail-safe that minimizes the risk of significant harm.

Offer Consistent Remedies or Appeals. Agencies must ensure that individuals affected by AI-enabled decisions have access to a timely human review and a chance to appeal any negative impacts, when appropriate.
To the extent consistent with law and governmentwide policy, each agency must publicly release a summary describing each individual determination and waiver, as well its justification.

Agencies must implement appropriate mitigations and ensure proper system and use documentation; and where possible, develop processes enabling traceability and transparency in this evaluation.

Agencies must proactively share across the Federal Government their custom-developed code-including models and model weights-whether agency developed or procured, for AI applications in active use, except in the circumstances described in paragraphs A through D below.
Agencies, where practicable, must also release and maintain AI code as open source software in a public repository 15 unless the: A. sharing of the code is restricted by law or regulation

Each agency (except for the Department of Defense and the Intelligence Community) must inventory its AI use cases at least annually, submit the inventory to 0MB, and post a public version on the agency's website.
For AI systems, agencies must continue to follow applicable authorization to operate requirements from 0MB Circular No. A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource.

Within 270 days of the issuance of this memorandum, agencies must revisit and update where necessary their internal policies on IT infrastructure ( e.g., software tools, use of open source software, libraries, and code for AI development, software deployment and platform modernization), data

cybersecurity (e.g., information system authorizations, continuous monitoring, continuous authorizations for Al), and privacy to align with this memorandum, Executive Order 14179, Executive Order 13960, and with applicable law.

within 180 days of the issuance of this memorandum or any update to this memorandum, and every two years thereafter until 2036, each agency must submit to 0MB and post publicly on the agency's website either a plan to achieve consistency with this memorandum, or a written determination that the agency does not use and does not anticipate using covered AL

CAIOs must centrally track waivers, reassess them if there are significant changes to the conditions or context in which the AI is used, and within 30 days of granting or revoking any waiver, report to 0MB on the scope, justification, and evidence supporting that action.
If a particular high-impact use case is not compliant with the minimum practices then the agency must safely discontinue use of the AI functionality.

When the high-impact AI is not performing at an appropriate level, agencies must have a plan to discontinue its use until actions are taken to achieve compliance with this memorandum. If proper risk mitigation is not possible, agencies must cease the use of the AI.

Within 365 days of the issuance of this memorandum, agencies must document implementation of the minimum practices in Section 4(b) of this memorandum for highimpact uses of AI and be prepared to report them to 0MB, as part of periodic accountability reviews, the annual AI use case inventory, or upon request as determined
CAIOs may revisit any determinations made within their agency to conclude that an AI use case is considered "high-impact" and must be subject to the minimum risk management practices at any time.

This section provides agencies with recommendations for the responsible procurement of AI capabilities to facilitate compliance with the minimum risk management practices for highimpact AI use cases detailed in Section 4.
Consistent with applicable law, it is the policy of the United States to buy American and to maximize the use of AI products and services that are developed and produced in the United States.

enforcement_authorities: Heads of covered Executive Branch departments and agencies (including independent regulatory agencies)
Chief AI Officer Council (chaired by OMB)
compliance_deadlines: Within 60 days of 2025-04-03 (2025-06-02): Each agency must retain or designate a Chief AI Officer (CAIO) and notify OMB within 30 days of any subsequent change or vacancy

Within 90 days of 2025-04-03 (2025-07-02): Each CFO Act agency must convene an Agency AI Governance Board; OMB must convene the interagency Chief AI Officer Council (sunsetting after 5 years unless extended)
Within 180 days of 2025-04-03 (2025-09-30): Each CFO Act agency (excluding DoD and IC) must develop and publicly post an Agency AI Strategy
Within 180 days of 2025-04-03 (2025-09-30) and every two years thereafter until 2036: Each agency must submit to OMB and publicly post an agency compliance plan or written non-use determination
Within 270 days of 2025-04-03 (2025-12-29): Each agency must update internal IT, data, cybersecurity, and privacy policies and develop a Generative AI acceptable-use policy

Within 365 days of 2025-04-03 (2026-04-03): Each agency (excluding IC) must implement and document Section 4(b) minimum risk management practices for high-impact AI (or discontinue non-compliant functionality) and publicly report determinations and waivers

Annually (and within 30 days of waiver grant/revocation or significant modifications): Agencies must submit to OMB and publicly release annual AI Use Case Inventories (excluding DoD and IC), annually recertify CAIO waivers, and report waiver grants/revocations to OMB within 30 days
penalties_summary: Enforced through executive compliance directives and mandatory discontinuation rather than statutory fines: agencies must safely discontinue or cease operating any high-impact AI functionality that does not comply with Section 4(b) minimum risk management practices unless a non-delegable CAIO written waiver is issued, recertified annually, publicly summarized, and reported to OMB within 30 days; agencies are subject to OMB periodic accountability reviews and public reporting of compliance plans and AI use case inventories.
implementation_notes: Issued April 3, 2025 by OMB Director Russell T. Vought pursuant to EO 14179, the AI in Government Act of 2020, and the Advancing American AI Act, rescinding and replacing OMB Memorandum M-24-10. Applies across executive agencies and independent regulatory agencies (excluding National Security Systems, with Intelligence Community carve-outs). Combines pro-innovation mandates (public AI strategies, mandatory government-wide sharing of custom-developed AI models/weights and open-source code release with 4 carve-outs, delegated risk acceptance) with binding governance structures (CAIOs, AI Governance Boards, CAIO Council) and 7 mandatory minimum risk management practices for 'high-impact AI' across 15 presumed high-impact categories (pre-deployment testing, AI Impact Assessments with internal independent review, ongoing monitoring, operator training, human oversight/fail-safes, human appeals/remedies, and public consultation).
